meta.purpose: Fire when the Risk Reasoning Agent finishes an assessment for a bridge, then invoke the Alert & Escalation service entrypoint (A901) with that {bridge_id, cycle_id} scope. One alert run per finalized assessment. GLUE ONLY — contains NO alert decision or judgment logic: no recipient routing, no approval gate, no message check, no send/escalate ladder (Constitution III: modularity; n8n moves data, the Python service makes every decision and owns the single human-approval chokepoint).  [n8n/Neon live verification deferred — none locally.]
meta.invokes: src/agents/alert_escalation/service.py :: run_alert (exposed over HTTP by the alert deployment) — one call per finalized assessment, per bridge
meta.decision_logic: none — every decision (which recipients, which channel, whether a human must approve, whether to withhold, when to close/escalate) lives in the Python service (A901), never here; n8n only forwards the scope and routes on the structured ok flag
meta.mode: fire-and-notify (async) — a gated alert may wait on a human approval or a delivery/ack that takes minutes, so this workflow does not block for it; the service enqueues the run and completion/close is reconciled via separate callbacks, not held open by n8n
meta.upstream: Risk Reasoning Agent assessment-available signal (Risk posts {bridge_id, cycle_id} to this webhook when its assessment for the bridge is persisted)
meta.callbacks: provider delivery receipts and human acknowledgements arrive on a separate callback webhook and are forwarded to the service to advance delivery_state (out-of-band reconciliation) — transport only, no interpretation here
meta.chokepoint: the alert service is the system's SINGLE real-world-action chokepoint (Principle I); this glue adds NO un-gated dispatch path of its own — it only invokes the gated service and never sends a notification itself
meta.out_of_scope: no notification is composed or sent here, and no approval is granted here — the gated Python service owns all of that (FR-5); this workflow only kicks off the run and forwards reconciliation callbacks

nodes.name: Risk Assessment Available
nodes.notes: Fires when the Risk Reasoning Agent finishes an assessment for one bridge and posts {bridge_id, cycle_id}. No inspection of the assessment contents here — the scope is forwarded as-is.

nodes.name: Invoke Alert & Escalation (A901)
nodes.notes: POST the {bridge_id, cycle_id} scope to the Python service entrypoint, which enqueues the run and returns quickly (fire-and-notify — n8n does not wait for a human approval or a delivery/ack). Retries the TRIGGER/invoke up to 3x on transport failure (Constitution IV: reliability). Redelivery is safe — the service is idempotent per assessment version (FR-10: supersede, not duplicate). The service returns a structured summary; n8n does not interpret its contents.

nodes.name: Run Accepted?
nodes.notes: Branch on the service's structured ok flag ONLY — never on the resolved tier, the delivery/escalation state, or the outcome contents. Any routing on those internals is the service's job, not this glue workflow's.

parameters.content: Run invocation failed at the service boundary (ok=false). Log + alert ops. The error detail is in {{ $json.error }}. No retry here — the HTTP node already retried transport; an ok=false is a structured result, not a transport fault.

Run accepted by the service (alert_dispatches + decision_log are written by the service). Nothing further for n8n to do here; a gated run may still be awaiting a human approval, and delivery/ack reconciliation arrives on the separate callback webhook below.

nodes.name: Delivery / Ack Callback
nodes.notes: Provider delivery receipts and human acknowledgements land here (out-of-band) and are forwarded to the service to advance delivery_state. Transport only — n8n does not decide anything about the reconciliation.

nodes.name: Forward Reconciliation (A901)
nodes.notes: Forward the receipt/ack to the service, which advances the row's delivery_state and re-resolves the escalation close. n8n forwards the callback payload as-is; the state transition is validated by the service's delivery state machine (A702), never here.
